entries.semantic_law: Return the unique finite factor list (l1,...,lk) such that concat(li)=w; all li are Lyndon (strictly lexicographically smaller than every proper nonempty suffix); and l1 >= l2 >= ... >= lk under explicit lexicographic 0<1. For empty source return []. No dependence on physical packing, phoneme ordering or hardware transport.
falsifiers: Returning a shortest repeated primitive root (e.g. 01010 -> 01010) instead of the ordered factor list is wrong.
Allowing increasing factors l_i<l_(i+1) violates the theorem's canonical ordering.
Factoring by a hidden phoneme collation rather than explicit D1 order 0<1 changes identity.
Treating nonempty '00' as a Lyndon component is invalid: it equals a proper suffix only lexically larger, and is not primitive.

entries.semantic_law: Compute all same-source one-step peaks arising from overlapping (including nested) occurrences of any pair of left sides. Each critical pair is joinable iff its two descendants share at least one reachable normal form under the same rules. Because every rule strictly shortens finite words, termination is proved by exact length. Then all critical pairs joinable is equivalent to confluence of the entire finite string rewrite relation (critical pair criterion + Newman's lemma). Return CONFLUENT or a concrete NONCONFLUENT witness: source, two branches, and separately reachable normal-form sets with empty intersection. Wording does not imply that a nonconfluent ruleset lacks individual common normal forms for other starting words.

positive_witnesses.reason: 00→0 is length-decreasing; overlapping runs of zeros converge
critical peak 010 reduces to 00 by either branch
010 can yield 00 or 01 and subsequently 0; direct normal-form witness may vary, compute oracle, don't assert exact branches blindly
no redex, reflexive closure is confluent

falsifiers: Never count disjoint non-overlapping redex occurrences as unjoinable critical conflicts; the two orders commute.
Two peaks may differ immediately yet be joinable later; comparing only first descendants is unsound.
Identical left sides with distinct right sides yield a critical peak; omitting containment or same-position overlaps misses a real conflict.
Do not invoke termination/Newman's lemma for length-preserving, length-growing, cyclic or unrestricted higher-order rewrite systems.
Do not return a nonconfluence witness without two reachable branches whose normal-form sets are disjoint.
entries.argument_shape: (ordered finite list of (nonempty-binary-lhs, strictly-shorter-binary-rhs))->CONFLUENT or NONCONFLUENT(witness)

entries.semantic_law: For n>=1, return D1 TRUE=1 iff length(word)=2^n AND the cyclic windows word[i],...,word[(i+n-1) mod 2^n] over all starts i∈[0,2^n) are pairwise distinct (equivalently cover all 2^n possible n-bit strings exactly once). Return D1 FALSE=0 for any well-typed word failing length or uniqueness. Invalid non-D1 data or n<=0 is a domain error, never a sneaky TRUE.

positive_witnesses.why: changed bit creates duplicate cyclic n-window
extra delimiter/bit changes required exact length
empty word never has required length
primitive 01 repetition does not cover all 2-bit patterns

falsifiers: Counting only linear substrings without wrap-around rejects valid 0011 at n=2
Accepting length 2^n with duplicate n-bit windows mistakes length for universal coverage
Treating a repeated primitive block as sufficient wrongly accepts 0101 at n=2
Treating word rotations as semantically different wrongly rejects 10001011 at n=3
Using an LFSR period alone without the all-zero state can miss one n-bit window
